question: A 2-week-old male newborn is brought to the physician because his mother has noticed her son has occasional bouts of ""turning blue in the face"" while crying. He also tires easily and sweats while feeding. He weighed 2150 g (4 lb 11 oz) at birth and has gained 200 g (7 oz). The baby appears mildly cyanotic. Examination shows a 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the left upper sternal border. A single S2 is present. An echocardiography confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following factors is the main determinant of the severity of this patient's cyanosis?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cyanosis in a newborn" -> "Murmur heard over the left upper sternal border" -> "Echocardiography confirms diagnosis" -> "Congenital heart defect" -> "Severity of cyanosis determined by the degree of mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood" -> "Atrial septal defect" -> 80%

enhanced_information: The severity of cyanosis in this patient is mainly determined by the degree of mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. The presence of an atrial septal defect is the main determinant in this case, leading to about 80% likelihood of causing the cyanosis. Ventricular septal defect follows with a 70% likelihood. Right ventricular outflow obstruction, left ventricular outflow obstruction, and right ventricular hypertrophy are not the main determinants of the severity of cyanosis in this patient.
